question: Report of the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) of March 2023 on Euroins Romania
Parliament’s website proclaims that ‘Parliament ensures a wide range of transparency measures [...] are in place to allow citizens to follow its debates and decisions’.

In its response to Written Question E-003294/2023 on the Euroins Romania case, the Commission suggests that ‘the Chairperson of EIOPA may be requested to hold confidential oral discussions with relevant participants of the competent committee of the European Parliament’.
Any such ‘confidential’ discussions would be the very antithesis of the transparency required ‘to allow citizens to follow [Parliament’s] debates and decisions’.

Against this background, I would like to ask once more whether the Commission is going to carry out an open, transparent and rigorous review of the EIOPA report of March 2023 on Euroins Romania, including how it was prepared, the source of the data used in its preparation and the accuracy of its conclusions, and whether it is planning make the findings of this review available to Parliament as a matter of urgency.
